verdict.rationale: Bento's docs show it ingests traces over OpenTelemetry. You can point a standard OTel exporter at one Bento endpoint with an auth header, even from TypeScript with no Bento package, and the Python SDK can feed an existing OTel pipeline. That covers the sending side natively. Nothing in the evidence shows traces leaving Bento over OTLP to other backends, and the docs say 'OpenTelemetry' without naming OTLP protocol or transport specifics. missing for 10: documented OTLP export/egress of traces from Bento (the 'receive' direction), explicit OTLP protocol and endpoint details (gRPC/HTTP), independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can send and receive traces over OpenTelemetry (OTLP) instead of a proprietary format

citations.quote: point its exporter at one endpoint with one auth header and the traces land in Bento. In TypeScript you can do this with no Bento package at all.
JavaScript's OpenTelemetry exporters can emit JSON, so you can send traces to Bento without installing any Bento package.
Wire it into an OpenTelemetry pipeline directly when you already have one configured, and skip the analytics layer entirely.
Every span from every framework, captured over OpenTelemetry.
